correctness.rationale: For every height-two incidence algebra the convolution formula on one edge has only its two endpoint terms. The diagonal-entry idempotent condition forces a strict entry to vanish on equal endpoint bits. The proposed source/sink diagonal factorization constructs two actual idempotents for every allowed support profile over arbitrary fields, and the allowed locus is a submonoid. Fixing a diagonal-one set yields q^(m-i_G(S)) elements, giving the exact generating function. The highest powers in idempotent and product counts are controlled respectively by proper two-colorings and independent sets. The UT3 rank-two Jordan nilpotent has an explicit three-idempotent factorization and cannot be a two-factor product by rank and diagonal support. A standalone script exhaustively verifies these implications in seven height-two finite-field configurations and two UT3 cases; the proof rather than experiments establishes unrestricted quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The full-text 2022 incidence-monoid study analyzes components of the idempotent variety and products inside orthodox antichain submonoids, not the two-factor product locus generated by all idempotents in the full ambient incidence monoid. The latter locus contains nilpotents and is therefore not implied by the orthodox-submonoid result. A 2024 idempotent-generator study concerns algebra-generation number; an unrestricted-transformation factorization theorem does not preserve incidence-algebra support. Searches for exact and equivalent structural statements showed no directly covering result in inspected material. The independence polynomial and cut count are standard; the claimed novelty lies in their structural realization by the complete product monoid. Publication priority remains subject to residual specialized-literature risk.
residual_risks: Full text of the 2024 Kolegov paper was not accessible; its abstract indicates an algebra-generator-number question but cannot rule out an incidental special result.
A more general matrix-semigroup theorem on products of idempotents inside upper-triangular or structural-matrix subalgebras could subsume the normal form.
No claim of exhaustive global literature coverage or independent mathematical validation is made.

value.rationale: The product locus generated by idempotents of a natural incidence monoid is a structural invariant, and the theorem completely classifies it for every height-two poset and every field, with explicit two-factor witnesses. The independent-set polynomial emerges as the leading exact diagonal-support enumerator over finite fields, so the result connects a nontrivial semigroup-generational condition to a recognized graph invariant across all bipartite posets. The simple three-chain supplies a sharp structural boundary and rules out a naive extension. These features supply value beyond isolated finite counts or elementary restatements.
